newsitem.title: USA: RTRS-Foster's keen on winery purchases.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Foster's keen on winery purchases.

text.p: Chuffed with the purchase of Mildara Blass and Rothbury wineries this year, Foster's Brewing Group Ltd chief executive Ted Kunkel said on Wednesday the company was on the lookout for further acquisitions.
"Should acquisitions become available, they will be readily pursued on one condition; that they surpass our basic financial hurdles," he told the McIntosh Securities Investment Conference here.
The Mildara Blass and Rothbury purchases cost Foster's A$532 million and the brewer also took on A$119 million in debt.

"The strategic highlight of the past year, was the switch from the low yielding brewing business in the U.K. (Courage which was sold in August 1995) to the growth oriented wine business," Kunkel said.
Foster's plans to swiftly expand the Mildara business.
"The strategic plan which Mildara is currently implementing is aimed at doubling its contribution from just under A$50 million over five years, with moderate capital and organic growth," Kunkel said.
Mildara Blass has a four per cent market share in Australia and a 25 per cent share in the premium category with a third of its total sales offshore.
The company contributed A$16 million in earnings before interest and tax in 1995/96, with domestic volume up three percent compared with a slight decline for the overall industry.
Foster's acquired Mildara in February this year.

The 1996 vintage produced record tonnages for the Australian wine industry, Foster's said in late August, including Mildara Blass which would be in a good position to satisfy projected demand in the future, including that for red wines.

The presence of Foster's in the competitive industry coincided with a boom year for Australian winemakers, who achieved strong profits and surging share prices, for the few who have not yet been taken over.
"We believe the wine sector will continue to outperform the All Ordinaries ... the immediate outlook for the industry is positive," stockbroker J.B Were & Son said in a recent report.
Strong sales in existing export markets, new market potential, and growing domestic demand for bottled wine were factors driving earnings growth, Were said.

The industry is dominated by four key players: Southcorp Wines, part of diversified manufacturer Southcorp Holdings Ltd , Mildara Blass, a unit of Foster's, rance-based Pernod Ricard's Orlando Wyndham, and the only major pure wine play, BRL Hardy Ltd.
